title: Ines and the Echo Anew
premise: Xanthe Villalobos has spent eleven years alone in the Svalbard seed vault, recording the decay of a colony that Earth's warring factions abandoned. When the deep-space ship Meridian returns with its crew aged backward into children, Xanthe becomes their reluctant guardian — and discovers the ship carries a peace protocol both governments will kill to bury. As hunters close in on the vault, Xanthe must choose between the duty of silence they inherited from their mother and the love growing for the crew's youngest survivor, now an old soul in a young body. In the end, Xanthe broadcasts the message to both worlds, ending the war at the cost of the vault and their own anonymity, and finds belonging not in a place but in the family that chooses to stay.
about_author: Mara Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing agricultural collections in northern research stations before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things alive.

chapters.title: The Long Inventory
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A day in the vault: checking seeds, logging failures, speaking to a recorder no one answers. Establishes ritual, loneliness, and the dying colony below ground. Emotional beat: devotion curdling into grief.

chapters.title: What Mother Left
chapters.summary: Xanthe finds their late mother's sealed instructions: if anyone comes, say nothing, protect the collection first. Flashbacks to her departure. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: A Light in the Ice
chapters.summary: Radar pings something descending through the polar night. Xanthe watches the Meridian crash-land on the glacier, torn between hiding and helping. Emotional beat: fear versus curiosity.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Xanthe reaches the wreck and finds twenty-three crew members aged backward into children with adult memories intact. Their captain, Odile, is now nine years old. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Mouths
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, practical panic: rationing food, converting storage bays into dormitories. The children begin tending the seeds with skills they shouldn't have yet. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hold
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the Meridian's cargo: a decryption key proving both governments engineered the war's famine together. She asks Xanthe to help broadcast it. Xanthe refuses, citing mother's orders. Emotional beat: duty colliding with conscience.

chapters.title: Small Hands, Old Eyes
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Odile. She navigates childhood — tantrums she resents, a body that won't obey — while watching Xanthe and forming a fragile alliance. Emotional beat: dignity under humiliation.

chapters.title: Signals in the Snow
chapters.summary: A scout drone passes overhead. Someone knows the Meridian fell. Xanthe scrambles the vault's camouflage systems, using tricks their mother taught them. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The First Hunter
chapters.summary: A government survey team arrives under pretense of rescue. Xanthe lies to their faces while the children hide among the seed racks. One child, Ivo, nearly gives them away. Emotional beat: terror managed through performance.

chapters.title: Ivo's Garden
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude. Ivo, the youngest, plants a forbidden garden in the vault's greenhouse; Xanthe catches him and, instead of punishing him, helps. Emotional beat: love taking root against rules.

chapters.title: What the Archive Knows
chapters.summary: Digging through mother's records, Xanthe learns she helped design the vault as a failsafe — the broadcast array was always meant to carry exactly this message. Her silence was a contingency, not cowardice. Emotional beat: reinterpreting inheritance.

chapters.title: The Second Ship
chapters.summary: Two military vessels enter orbit. The team on the ice turns hostile, demanding access to the vault. Xanthe triggers lockdown, sealing themselves inside with the children. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Siege of Seeds
chapters.summary: The besiegers cut power. The children, drawing on crew training, jury-rig geothermal taps while Xanthe negotiates through the door. Odile collapses — her reversed aging is accelerating. Emotional beat: unity under pressure, new dread.

chapters.title: Odile's Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The reversal will erase her memories entirely within weeks unless the ship's medical bay — buried in the wreck — is reached. She entrusts the mission's memory to Xanthe. Emotional beat: intimacy forged by mortality.

chapters.title: Across the Glacier
chapters.summary: Xanthe and two children trek to the wreck through a storm to reach the medical bay, pursued by the survey team. They succeed but are spotted. Emotional beat: courage as a series of small decisions.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo, terrified, contacts the besiegers offering the key in exchange for mercy. Confronted, he breaks down; his betrayal reveals the vault's weak entrance. Emotional beat: forgiveness harder than anger.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Soldiers storm the vault. Xanthe floods the seed corridors with nitrogen to stop them without killing, gambling the collection itself. Hand-to-hand chaos in the dark stacks. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the sacred.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Room
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe, Odile, and Ivo reach the hidden array. Soldiers breach behind them. Odile, half-erased, recites the decryption key from memory as it fades; Xanthe transmits the truth to both worlds mid-breach. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved in action.

chapters.title: Silence Afterward
chapters.summary: The transmission lands. Fighting stops mid-motion as soldiers receive orders to stand down; some weep. The vault is half-flooded, much of the collection lost. Emotional beat: hollow victory, exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Delegations arrive. Xanthe, once invisible, must testify about the colony's abandonment and the famine's origins. Odile, now barely remembering, sits beside them. Emotional beat: being seen at last.

chapters.title: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Months later: the surviving seeds are redistributed to reclaiming colonies. Ivo's greenhouse garden becomes the vault's heart. Odile begins again as a child truly, with Xanthe as guardian. Emotional beat: grief transformed into stewardship.

chapters.title: Ines and the Echo Anew
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Xanthe's recorder running again — but now the logs are letters to the children, to Odile, to whoever comes next. The echo their mother started continues, changed. Xanthe stays, no longer alone. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, inheritance redeemed.
